summary:
Be An Earth System Trend Detective!

Our project aims to create an interactive tool to identify, analyze, and visualize changes in Earth's environmental systems. It is part of the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, focusing on Earth Science and Software.

Environmental variables such as temperature, rainfall, vegetation, ocean conditions, and water levels change over time. Their trends can differ between regions: a variable may increase in one place and decrease in another. Understanding large environmental datasets can be challenging.

Our tool will explore NASA Giovanni, Hydrology Time Series, NASA AppEEARS, NOAA Climate Data Online, KNMI Climate Explorer, and the SWOT Mission. Users can select variables and time periods, examine historical measurements, and compare regions.

Graphs, charts, and interactive maps will display results. Trend-detection methods will identify increasing, decreasing, or stable patterns. Statistical analysis will help assess whether trends are significant rather than random variations.

The project will answer five questions: What is changing? Where? How much? How is it changing over time? Are the changes statistically significant?

The expected outcome is a dashboard that transforms scientific data into visual insights. It can help students, researchers, and environmental scientists understand patterns across our changing planet.

Our vision is to make Earth science data easier to explore and help everyone become an Earth System Trend Detective!
details: Project Details – Be An Earth System Trend Detective! Our project, Be An Earth System Trend Detective!, is an interactive platform designed to identify, analyze, and visualize environmental changes across the Earth. It helps users understand what is changing, where it is changing, how much it is changing, and whether those changes are statistically significant. How It Works: The platform uses Earth science datasets from NASA and other scientific organizations. Users can select environmental variables such as temperature, rainfall, vegetation, and water levels, choose geographical regions, and examine changes over different time periods. The system processes the selected data using time-series analysis and statistical trend detection methods. It identifies increasing, decreasing, and stable trends and presents the results through interactive graphs, charts, and geographical maps. Tools and Technologies: Our project draws on resources such as NASA Giovanni, NASA AppEEARS, Hydrology Time Series, NOAA Climate Data Online, KNMI Climate Explorer, and the SWOT Mission. Python and GIS-based tools are potential technologies for data processing and visualization. The final programming languages, software stack, and hardware will depend on the implementation. Benefits and Impact: The platform makes complex environmental datasets easier to understand. It can support students, researchers, and environmental scientists in studying climate patterns, comparing geographical regions, identifying environmental trends, and understanding changes in Earth's interconnected systems. It can also support environmental monitoring and scientific research. Creativity and Innovation: The creative aspect of our project is bringing multiple Earth science data resources, geographical visualization, and statistical analysis together in one platform. Instead of simply displaying environmental measurements, it acts as a trend detective by identifying patterns and explaining how environmental conditions change across different locations and time periods. Factors Considered: We considered data availability, accuracy, reliability, geographical differences, historical trends, missing measurements, statistical significance, and ease of use. We also considered the importance of presenting scientific results in a simple and understandable format. Our ultimate goal is to transform complex Earth science data into meaningful insights and help people better understand our changing planet.
